summary.business: Biocon Limited is a public limited company incorporated and domiciled in India, engaged in the manufacture of biotechnology products and research services, with its registered office in Bengaluru, Karnataka and shares listed on the BSE and NSE. The group operates across three business lines described in the Board's Report - Generics, Biosimilars and CRDMO - and serves patients globally through subsidiaries that develop, manufacture, commercialise and distribute pharmaceuticals, biopharmaceuticals and biologics in the United States, Europe, Malaysia and other geographies. During FY26 the Company fully integrated its material subsidiary Biocon Biologics Limited, standing as a single unified organisation - OneBiocon - with effect from April 01, 2026.

Elevate.' and the BioLead leadership development architecture spanning five leadership tiers and four development levels|Biocon's stated capital-allocation intent during FY26 was to consolidate ownership of its biologics platform: after evaluating multiple strategic options for Biocon Biologics Limited - including an IPO of its equity shares and other restructuring alternatives such as a merger - the Board concluded that fully integrating BBL through acquisition of minority stakes was the most efficient and value-accretive path, and it proposes to acquire the residual stake so BBL becomes a wholly-owned subsidiary. That consolidation was funded through equity issuance (Qualified Institutions Placements and a preferential allotment of Biocon Limited shares to the BBL selling shareholders as share-swap consideration), alongside use of commercial paper and early full redemption of outstanding non-convertible debentures, reflecting a preference for de-levering and simplifying the capital structure. currentContext.expansion: Biocon's Generics manufacturing network comprises six API facilities across Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Visakhapatnam, supported by formulations facilities in India and the United States. The headline expansion milestone of FY26 was the commissioning and inauguration of Biocon's first Oral Solid Dosage (OSD) manufacturing facility in the United States, at Cranbury, New Jersey - a site that enables local manufacturing and direct supply for the U.S. generics portfolio, complements the Indian formulations network, reduces supply-chain dependencies and improves speed-to-market and customer responsiveness. The Cranbury facility received a U.S. FDA Establishment Inspection Report with a Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI) outcome following an FY26 inspection, confirming GMP compliance and readiness for commercial operations. Alongside this, the Company is developing injectable and device-assembly capabilities in Bengaluru to support the growing share of complex and specialty formulations, and its formulations footprint spans oral solid dosages in Bengaluru and Cranbury covering potent and non-potent products, plus injectables and complex drug-device combinations such as vials, pre-filled syringes, pens and auto-injectors. Capital expenditure during the year was primarily directed towards capacity expansion and capability enhancement, including commissioning of the U.S. OSD facility and investments in injectables, peptides and complex formulations, while R&D spend stayed focused on sustaining the pipeline across APIs, formulations and GLP-1s. Investments in capacity, process optimisation and operational efficiency continue to be aligned with medium-term demand visibility and portfolio complexity. On the corporate-structure side, the Company fully integrated Biocon Biologics Limited during FY26, holding ~99% of BBL on a fully diluted basis as on March 31, 2026 and operating as a single unified organisation - OneBiocon - with effect from April 01, 2026, with a proposal to acquire the remaining ~1% so that BBL becomes a wholly-owned subsidiary.

risks.risk: Financial risk - meeting obligations of banks and PE investors
risks.note: Classified as a Strategic risk and rated Low at residual level. Mitigation rests on an optimised capital structure and financial leverage, compliance with investor and debt obligations, and fund raising that enabled settlement with PE investors and bankers; the minority shareholding in Biocon Biologics Limited was acquired, making it a 100% subsidiary of Biocon.

Classified as a Regulatory risk and rated Medium at residual level. Delays can hold up launch of new products and lifecycle management of existing products, directly affecting timely launches in key markets, revenue generation and market share. Mitigation includes maintaining continued 'Voluntary Action Indicated' (VAI) status for manufacturing sites in India and Malaysia.

risks.risk: Commercial risk - failure to meet forecasted business growth plans
risks.note: Classified as a Strategic risk and rated Medium at residual level. Missing growth plans in the markets where the Company operates would adversely impact overall growth and business plans. Mitigated through comprehensive landscape analysis covering competition and market dynamics before entering any new market, managing timely launch of new products, and partnering with local entities for compliance with local requirements.

risks.risk: Infotech and cybersecurity - inadequate defence mechanism against cyber-attacks
risks.note: Classified as a Technological risk and rated Medium at residual level. Data loss or breach through employees or external parties carries reputational and financial impact, and downtime disrupts operations.

Identified as one of the top risk themes monitored by the Risk Management Committee; the Company's integrated risk approach explicitly encompasses both business risks and ESG-related risks across the Company, its stakeholders and the value chain.

A distinct category within the Company's risk universe; the risk library spans Sectoral, Strategic, Information Technology, Catastrophic, ESG/Sustainability, Geo-political, Regulatory and Statutory, and Executional/Operational risks, from which the key risks that matter are selected on impact and likelihood.

Compliance risks are named among the top risk themes identified by the ERM function; the risk universe carries a dedicated Regulatory and Statutory category, and improving compliance with good corporate governance guidelines, laws and regulations is a stated objective of the risk framework.

A dedicated category in the risk universe covering execution of business operations; the framework's objective is to ensure business operations continue uninterrupted, with catastrophic and sectoral risks also mapped in the risk library and monitored quarterly by the Risk Management Committee.

one-line thesis: Biocon completed its biosimilars-genetics integration, achieving 12% Q4 biosimilars growth and 23% EBITDA margin with $1.1B net debt down from $1.5B, positioning it for margin expansion in FY27 via U.S. launches of Bosaya/Aukelso and Aspart insulin, while free cash flow is now fully directed to debt reduction.
financial scorecard: revenue: +10% YoY (biosimilars +12%, generics +13% ex-lenalidomide); EBITDA/margin: ₹1,073cr (+29% adj), 23% margin (up 200bps YoY); PAT (rptd): ₹179cr; PAT (normalized): ₹179cr (no exceptionals); order book: not disclosed; net debt: ₹9,100cr (~$1.1B), down from $1.5B in Mar'25, with $75cr/quarter interest savings accruing
guidance: revenue growth: FY27 to see acceleration in 2H via new launches; margin: expanding via operating leverage in biosimilars (26% in Q4) and generics (8% in Q4, up 300bps qoq); order inflow: not guided; capex/commissioning: Malaysia DP line operational, DS doubling by FY26 end, no greenfield capex needed
segment / subsidiary detail: Biosimilars: ₹2,756cr revenue (+12% YoY), 26% EBITDA margin; Generics: ₹847cr revenue (+13% adj YoY), 8% EBITDA margin; CRDMO: ₹1,037cr revenue (+2% YoY), 25% EBITDA margin
growth verticals / optionality: U.S. launches of Bosaya™/Aukelso™ (denosumab) and Kirsty™ (insulin Aspart) in 2H FY27; liraglutide (gVictoza/gSaxenda) scaling in Europe; Yesafili™ (aflibercept) launch post-settlement in 2H FY27; peptide portfolio fungibility enabling cross-utilization
margins & cost dynamics: Biosimilars margin up to 26% due to revenue mix shift to U.S. and operating leverage; Generics margin improved 300bps qoq to 8% via volume and API/formulation mix; CRDMO margin stable at 25%; interest cost down ₹75cr/quarter from FY26 peak
capex / expansion: Malaysia drug product line operational; drug substance doubling to complete by FY26 end; minor debottlenecking in Bangalore; no greenfield capex planned; total capex phase complete
capital allocation: 100% of free cash flow directed to debt reduction; net debt down to $1.1B; no M&A or buybacks mentioned; R&D spend at 7% of biosimilars revenue
risks & watch-items: U.S. pricing pressure in medical benefit space; delayed regulatory approvals; currency volatility on dollar-denominated debt; competitive entry in GLP-1 generics
management quality / tone: Confident, execution-focused, disciplined; emphasized integration completion, deleveraging, and shift from investment to operating leverage; avoided quarter-on-quarter guidance, stressed long-term profitable growth
non-obvious takeaways: FDA’s new biosimilar pathway reduces R&D cost by 50% and accelerates timelines by 3–4 years — Biocon’s CMC expertise gives it structural advantage; insulin franchise now >$300M with 100% share in closed U.S. networks; no hedging on dollar debt due to natural hedge from dollar revenues

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.
